`Invoke-ADSurvey.ps1` is the canonical **Phase 1 (Discovery)** adapter for the
UIAO Active Directory → Entra ID modernization track. It performs a read-only
enumeration of an on-premises forest and emits one structured JSON object that
the UIAO AD adapter (`survey.py`) consumes directly.

It runs the **forest / tree / trust topology pass first**, before walking the OU
tree — deliberately. OrgPath is the DN-encoded organizational spine, and a
`distinguishedName` only carries meaning once you know the forest root, the
constituent domains (trees), and the trust boundaries that join them. So the
survey establishes that context up front, then descends into OUs, users,
service accounts, sites, and GPOs.

::: {.callout-important}
The survey output is a map of where your directory is weak — stale objects,
unconstrained-delegation accounts, cross-boundary trusts with SID filtering
disabled. Treat it as **Controlled**: keep input and output inside your
authorization boundary, share only with authorized personnel, and do not
publish raw findings.
:::

## Download

| Artifact | Version | SHA256 |
|---|---|---|
| [`Invoke-ADSurvey.ps1`](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/scripts/ad-survey/Invoke-ADSurvey.ps1) | 1.0 | `9b590c08158a40f8b7e0145329101580ec29e7575735985301f1d291d665701f` |

The script is served from its canonical home (`scripts/ad-survey/` in the repo)
because it is also the runtime artifact the UIAO AD adapter invokes — one file,
no drift. Use the **Download raw file** button on the GitHub page, then verify
integrity after download:

```powershell
Get-FileHash .\Invoke-ADSurvey.ps1 -Algorithm SHA256
# compare the output to the SHA-256 above before running
```

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Notes |
|---|---|
| PowerShell 5.1 or 7.x | `survey.py` invokes it via `pwsh`; interactively either host works. |
| RSAT: Active Directory module for Windows PowerShell | Provides `Get-ADForest`, `Get-ADDomain`, `Get-ADDomainController`, `Get-ADOrganizationalUnit`, `Get-ADUser`, `Get-ADComputer`, `Get-ADTrust`, `Get-ADReplicationSite*`. The script does `Import-Module ActiveDirectory` and stops if it is missing. |
| RSAT: Group Policy Management *(optional)* | Provides the `GroupPolicy` module. If absent, GPO enumeration is skipped with a warning and the rest of the survey still completes. |
| Domain user with read access | Default `Authenticated Users` permission is sufficient for the read-only enumeration in most environments. |
| Forest-wide reachability | The topology pass (`Get-ADForest` / `Get-ADTrust` / cross-domain `Get-ADDomain`) needs to reach the forest root and each domain. On a host that can only see one domain, topology degrades gracefully to an empty `forest` block (a warning is written) and the OU/user/SA/site survey still runs. |

The survey is entirely read-only: it issues `Get-*` cmdlets only and writes
nothing back to the directory.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-Server` | `string` | Yes | Domain controller FQDN or IP to bind against. |
| `-BaseDN` | `string` | Yes | Forest root distinguished name, e.g. `DC=corp,DC=contoso,DC=com`. Scopes the OU/user/SA enumeration. |
| `-OutputJson` | `switch` | No | Emit the full JSON object to stdout (for `survey.py` or `ConvertFrom-Json`). When omitted, a human-readable summary table is printed instead. |
| `-IncludeComputers` | `switch` | No | Include computer-object enumeration. Off by default because it can be slow on large forests. |

The script also honours the standard `-Verbose` common parameter and logs each
discovery phase (topology, OUs, users, service accounts, sites, GPOs) with
counts.

## Usage

### Emit JSON for the UIAO adapter

```powershell
.\Invoke-ADSurvey.ps1 -Server dc01.corp.contoso.com -BaseDN "DC=corp,DC=contoso,DC=com" -OutputJson
```

This is the shape `survey.py::_run_powershell_survey()` calls — it pipes the
JSON to `_merge_ps_output()`, which lifts the forest topology counts and the OU
and user inventories into the survey report.

### Interactive summary (no JSON)

```powershell
.\Invoke-ADSurvey.ps1 -Server dc01.corp.contoso.com -BaseDN "DC=corp,DC=contoso,DC=com"
```

Prints a console summary — the fastest way to eyeball forest scale before a
full run:

```text
=== UIAO AD Forest Survey Summary ===
Forest:          DC=corp,DC=contoso,DC=com
Forest name:     corp.contoso.com (mode Windows2016Forest)
Domains/Trees:   3
Domain Ctrls:    7
Site Links:      4
Trusts:          2 (1 SID-filtering risk)
OUs:             214
Users:           9842
Service Accts:   118 (6 ADCS-suspect)
Unconstrained:   3 delegation accounts
Computer Objs:   0 (0 stale)
Sites:           5 (1 stale/no-subnet)
GPOs:            187 (41 not modified 5+ years)
Existing OrgPath: 0 users already have extensionAttribute1
```

### Include computer objects

```powershell
.\Invoke-ADSurvey.ps1 -Server dc01.corp.contoso.com -BaseDN "DC=corp,DC=contoso,DC=com" -IncludeComputers -OutputJson
```

### Capture JSON to disk

```powershell
.\Invoke-ADSurvey.ps1 -Server dc01.corp.contoso.com -BaseDN "DC=corp,DC=contoso,DC=com" -OutputJson |
    Out-File -Encoding utf8 .\forest-survey.json
```

### The `forest` block

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name`, `forestMode`, `rootDomain` | Forest identity and functional level. |
| `domainCount`, `globalCatalogs` | Tree count and the GC inventory. |
| `fsmoRoles` | The five operations-master holders (Schema, Domain-Naming, PDC, RID, Infrastructure). |
| `domains[]` | Each tree/domain: DNS root, NetBIOS, domain mode, DN, per-domain FSMO holders, and an `isForestRoot` flag. |
| `domainControllers[]` | Every DC: site, IP, OS/version, GC and RODC status, and its FSMO roles. |
| `siteLinks[]` | Inter-site replication links with cost and frequency — the topology spine for multi-tree forests. |
| `trusts[]` | Every trust: direction, type, intra-forest vs. cross-boundary, and SID-filtering state. |

### Trust risk flag

Each trust carries a computed `sidFilteringRisk` boolean. It is `true` when the
trust is **cross-boundary** (`intraForest = false`) **and** SID filtering is
**not** quarantined — a SID-history privilege-escalation path you want to
remediate before migrating the forest. The survey surfaces it as an
observational count (`summary.riskyTrustCount`); it is not yet a blocking
governance finding.

## Integration patterns

### UIAO AD adapter (primary path)

`survey.py` prefers an in-process `ldap3` survey. When `ldap3` is unavailable —
or when you are running on a domain-joined Windows host — it falls back to this
script:

```text
survey.py::_run_powershell_survey()
  → pwsh -NonInteractive -File scripts/ad-survey/Invoke-ADSurvey.ps1 -Server … -BaseDN … -OutputJson
  → json.loads(stdout)
  → _merge_ps_output()   # lifts forest topology counts + OU/user inventories into ADSurveyReport
```

This is why the download links to `scripts/ad-survey/Invoke-ADSurvey.ps1` rather
than a copy under `docs/`: the published download and the adapter's runtime
dependency are the same file.

### Scheduled discovery

Run on a cadence under a managed service account with the read permissions
above, directing JSON at a path the Evidence Ledger pickup job watches:

```powershell
$action  = New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute 'pwsh.exe' `
    -Argument '-NoProfile -File C:\UIAO\Invoke-ADSurvey.ps1 -Server dc01.corp.contoso.com -BaseDN "DC=corp,DC=contoso,DC=com" -OutputJson' `
    -WorkingDirectory 'C:\UIAO'
$trigger = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Weekly -DaysOfWeek Sunday -At 2am
Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'UIAO-ADSurvey' `
    -Action $action -Trigger $trigger -User 'CORP\svc-uiao-survey' -RunLevel Highest
```

### Topology triage

For a fast forest/trust read in-session:

```powershell
$survey = .\Invoke-ADSurvey.ps1 -Server dc01.corp.contoso.com -BaseDN "DC=corp,DC=contoso,DC=com" -OutputJson | ConvertFrom-Json
$survey.forest.trusts | Where-Object sidFilteringRisk |
    Format-Table name, direction, trustType, sidFilteringQuarantined
```

## Tuning notes

- **`-IncludeComputers`** — left off by default; computer enumeration is the
  slowest pass on large estates. Add it only when you need the stale-device
  inventory (`computers[]` + `staleComputerCount`).
- **Forest reachability** — if topology comes back empty, the host can reach the
  bound domain but not the forest root or peer domains. Run from a host with
  line of sight to the forest root, or accept the OU/user/SA/site survey alone.
- **`-Server` selection** — bind to a domain controller in the domain that owns
  the `-BaseDN` you scope; cross-domain object enumeration relies on referrals.
